divider.text: Scope of Section 54G: Specified Assets Only

facts.text: Neither sale nor new purchase qualifies

beats.voice_sync_text: Section 54G clear aayi parayunnu: Capital Gain arose from transfer of machinery, plant, building, or land used for the purpose of an industrial undertaking situated in an urban area. Assessee 1 year before or 3 years after the date of transfer eligible assets purchase cheythal, deduction kittum.

quote.text: Where the capital gain arises from the transfer of a capital asset, being plant, machinery, land or building or any rights in building or land, used for the purpose of an industrial undertaking situated in an urban area... and the assessee has within a period of one year before or three years after the date on which the transfer took place purchased new machinery or plant or acquired building or land...
quote.emphasis: plant, machinery, land or building... 1 year before or 3 years after

context_bubble.note: Reinvestment Window: July 2026 acquisition satisfies the 'within 3 years after March 2026' requirement.

beats.voice_sync_text: Nammude total eligible investment pool ethrayanu? Land Rs 4 Lakh, Building Rs 7 Lakh, Plant & Machinery Rs 17 Lakh. Total Rs 28 Lakhs! Note cheyyuka, Furniture-nte Rs 2 Lakh ivide add cheyyan padilla. Ee Rs 28 Lakhs namukk STCG-kkum LTCG-kkum ethirayi set-off cheyyam.

Tax optimizationte golden trick ivideyanu! Act-il pro-rata set-off niyamam illa. Assessee-kk beneficial aaya reethiyil exemption exhaust cheyyam. Athukondu higher tax bracket ulla Short-term Capital Gain first wipe out cheyyanam. Building & Plant STCG total Rs 25 Lakhs poornnamayum Section 54G vechu Nil aakki. Balance Rs 3 Lakhs Land-nte Long-term Capital Gain-il ninnu kurachu. So, final taxable amount just Rs 2 Lakhs mathram!

rules.heading: Strict Asset Basket (Furniture Excluded)
rules.body: Section 54G applies strictly to Plant, Machinery, Land, and Building. Capital gains on Furniture cannot be exempted, and reinvestment in Furniture does not count towards the eligible investment.

rules.heading: Section 50 Deemed STCG is Eligible
rules.body: Even though Section 50 deems depreciable assets as Short-Term Capital Gains, Section 54G exemption is fully applicable against such deemed STCG (established in landmark jurisprudence and CBDT circulars).

rules.heading: Most Beneficial Set-Off Ordering
rules.body: The statute does not compel pro-rata apportionment. Always exhaust Section 54G exemption against Short-Term Capital Gains first (normal tax rate) before offsetting Long-Term Capital Gains (concessional 12.5% rate u/s 112).
